ch19.d.N: Number of gas molecules (disks) in the box
ch19.d.T: Temperature of the gas; sets the mean molecular kinetic energy $kT$ (2D)
ch19.d.L: Side length $L$ of the square box
ch19.d.init: Speed distribution of the molecules at the start
ch19.d.arrows: Velocity $\vec v$ arrow on every molecule
ch19.goal.sum: Pressure = time average of the impulses $2mv_x$ that many molecules deliver to the wall
ch19.goal.ideal: Compare the measured pressure with the ideal-gas prediction $pA = NkT$ (2D)
ch19.obs.J: Impulse $J$ delivered to the right wall: rises in steps, one per bounce; its mean slope is the mean force on the wall (dashed: ideal gas)
ch19.obs.fluct: The 10 ps moving average of the pressure fluctuates strongly; the average since the start, $J/(Lt)$, converges to the dashed line $NkT/A$
ch19.obs.N: Larger $N$: the pressure grows in proportion to $N$ and the relative fluctuations shrink
ch19.obs.T: Doubling the temperature: molecules move faster and hit more often, so the pressure doubles
ch19.obs.hist: Even when every molecule starts at the same speed, collisions turn the speed distribution into the 2D Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution (dashed)
ch19.assume.2d: 2D gas: pressure = force per unit wall length (mN/m = pN/nm), area $A = L^2$
ch19.assume.disk: Hard disks the size of helium atoms (diameter 0.26 nm, mass $6.65\times10^{-27}$ kg), perfectly elastic collisions, smooth walls
ch19.assume.dense: Because the disks take up area, the measured pressure is a little above the ideal-gas value: about 9 % at $N = 150$, $L = 15$ nm and about 4 % at the defaults ($N = 100$, $L = 20$ nm)
ch19.assume.win: During the first 10 ps both pressure plots divide the impulse so far by 10 ps, so they start from 0
